name: Sika
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Lewis, E.D. & Grimes, C.E. 1995. 'Sika', in Tryon (ed.), Comparative Austronesian Dictionary (sketch; plausibly covers stress); reachable pages had no stress statement

new_statements.quote: 4°. De klemtoon valt altijd op de voorlaatste lettergreep; behalve als anders aangegeven wordt. 5°. Het teeken ´ boven eene lettergreep beteekent dat op die lettergreep den klemtoon valt.
new_statements.translation: 4. The stress always falls on the penultimate syllable, except where indicated otherwise. 5. The sign ´ above a syllable means that the stress falls on that syllable.
new_statements.citation: Calon, L. F. 1890. Woordenlijstje van het dialect van Sikka (Midden-Flores). Tijdschrift voor Indische Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde 33: 501-530 (preface, p. 501, rules 4-5).
new_statements.locator: p. 501 (PDF leaf 524 of the archive.org volume scan tijdschriftvoor02wetegoog), numbered preface rules 4° and 5°
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is penultimate by default; the wordlist marks with an acute the (lexical) exceptions where stress falls elsewhere.
new_statements.exceptions: Exceptions exist and are marked individually in the wordlist with an acute over the stressed syllable; no rule for them is given. Calon 1893 (TBG 35, p. 128-129) adds that mountain dwellers say 'lahing' with penultimate stress where the coast has 'lahein'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, citation forms in a Dutch-Sikkanese wordlist compiled by the Maumere parish priest; the dialect is that of Sikka/Maumere on the south-central coast ('dialect van Sikka, Midden-Flores'). An 1890 missionary source, so orthography-driven and pre-phonemic; the modern descriptions (Rosen 1986, Lewis & Grimes 1995, Fricke 2014) could not be opened to confirm.
new_statements.identity_note: Calon's 1890 wordlist describes the coastal Sikka/Maumere dialect ('dialect van Sikka, Midden-Flores'; Calon was parish priest at Maumere), i.e. sika1262 proper; Lewis 1982 (opened, no stress statement) treats the Tana Ai dialect (Sara Tana Ai) and Fricke 2014 (not opened) the Hewa variety, both sub-dialects of the same glottocode with no separate Glottolog languoid.

sources.citation: Calon, L. F. 1890. Woordenlijstje van het dialect van Sikka (Midden-Flores). Tijdschrift voor Indische Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde 33: 501-530 (preface, p. 501, rules 4-5).
sources.quote: 4°. De klemtoon valt altijd op de voorlaatste lettergreep; behalve als anders aangegeven wordt. 5°. Het teeken ´ boven eene lettergreep beteekent dat op die lettergreep den klemtoon valt.
sources.locator: p. 501 (PDF leaf 524 of the archive.org volume scan tijdschriftvoor02wetegoog), numbered preface rules 4° and 5°
sources.note: Preface rule 4 on p. 501: stress always falls on the penultimate syllable except where indicated otherwise; rule 5: an acute over a syllable marks stress on that syllable (exceptions marked in the wordlist).

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Owen Edwards. 2026 [Glottolog 2025]. The Austronesian languages of eastern Indonesia and Timor-Leste: Unravelling their prehistory and classification. Berlin: Language Science Press. 948 pp.
sources.note: Comparative work; states only the regional generalisation 'While penultimate stress is the normal rule for Wallacean languages, words with penultimate schwa can have stress on other syllables' (schwa section citing Sika via Lewis & Grimes 1995); no Sika-specific stress statement in the Sika passages.

sources.citation: Calon, L. F. 1893. Eenige opmerkingen over het dialect van Sikka, gevolgd door eenige bemerkingen op de vorige lijstjes, eenige spreekwijzen, enz. Tijdschrift voor Indische Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde 35: 129-199.
sources.note: Pronunciation notes on consonants and vowels; no general stress rule, only the remark that mountain dwellers say 'lahing' with stress on the penultimate syllable (coastal 'lahein'); a corrigendum refers back to the 1891 list's note on the stress sign.
